name: Halo 3 (MCC)

scale.why: speeds measured in Forge metres; scaled to 1.8 m taking the Spartan as about 7 ft (2.134 m, the H2EK player reference): 0.8435 m per Forge metre

speed.note: one player's measurement over the Forge grid; the 1.8 m rescale is an assumption

gravity.source: https://www.bungie.net/en/Forums/Post/3291870 (jump peak 245 % of the Spartan's height, 1.4 s in the air)
gravity.note: derived from the measured jump: rise = (245 - 100) % of 1.8 m = 2.61 m, g = 8 x rise / airtime^2

jump.note: take-off speed = 4 x rise / airtime = 4 x 2.61 / 1.4

grapple.note: no grapple (Halo Infinite adds the Grappleshot)

jumpHeight.note: 145 % of the player's height, scaled to 1.8 m; Quark: 1.22 m

mlgSpeed.note: MLG settings; the post's percentages for it disagree (110% in the settings list, 90% beside the measurement)

extras: slow, high jumps compared with arena shooters: the airtime (1.4 s) is about twice Quark's
notes: One player's measurements (bungie.net, 2011): run speed over the Forge grid, jump height in hundredths of the Spartan's height and airtime. Gravity and jump speed are derived from the height and airtime (estimates), and everything is rescaled to a 1.8 m player taking the Spartan as 7 ft.

sources.title: bungie.net: classic Halo movement speed, jump height, gravity
H2EK: Player Statistics and Metrics (Spartan about 7 ft)
